facts.name: dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase
facts.summary: The protein encoded by this gene is a pyrimidine catabolic enzyme and the initial and rate-limiting factor in the pathway of uracil and thymidine catabolism. Mutations in this gene result in dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency, an error in pyrimidine metabolism associated with thymine-uraciluria and an increased risk of toxicity in cancer patients receiving 5-fluorouracil chemotherapy. Two transcript variants encoding different isoforms have been found for this gene. [provided by RefSeq, May 2009].

claims.text: The DPYD gene encodes the dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase protein, a pyrimidine catabolic enzyme.
Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase is the initial and rate-limiting factor in the pathway of uracil and thymidine catabolism.
Mutations in the DPYD gene result in dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency.
Two transcript variants encoding different isoforms of the dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase protein have been found for the DPYD gene.
